Main.sentence: The Islamic State ( IS ), [d] also known as the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant ( ISIL ), the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria ( ISIS ) and Daesh , is a transnational ___E:Salafi jihadist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salafi_jihadism)___ militant organisation   and an unrecognised ___E:quasi-state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quasi-state)___ .

IS occupied significant territory in ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq)___ and ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ in 2013, but lost most of it in 2017 and 2019. In 2014, the group proclaimed itself to be a worldwide ___E:caliphate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliphate)___ , and claimed religious and political authority over all ___E:Muslims U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims)___ worldwide, a claim not accepted by the vast majority of Muslims.

It is ___E:designated as a terrorist organisation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_designated_terrorist_groups)___ by the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ and many countries around the world, including ___E:Muslim countries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_world)___ .

By the end of 2015, its self-declared caliphate ruled an area with a population of about 12 million,  where they enforced their extremist interpretation of ___E:Islamic law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_law)___ , managed an annual budget exceeding US$1 billion, and commanded more than 30,000 fighters.

After a grinding conflict with American, Iraqi, and Kurdish forces, IS lost control of all its Middle Eastern territories by 2019, subsequently reverting to insurgency from remote hideouts while continuing its ___E:propaganda efforts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media_use_by_the_Islamic_State)___ .
These efforts have garnered a significant following in northern and ___E:Sahelian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahelian)___ Africa,   where IS still controls a significant territory.

Originating in the ___E:Jaish al-Ta'ifa al-Mansurah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaish_al-Ta%27ifa_al-Mansurah)___ founded by ___E:Abu Omar al-Baghdadi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Omar_al-Baghdadi)___ in 2004, the organisation (primarily under the ___E:Islamic State of Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq)___ name) affiliated itself with ___E:al-Qaeda in Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda_in_Iraq)___ and fought alongside them during the ___E:2003–2006 phase of the Iraqi insurgency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%932006_phase_of_the_Iraqi_insurgency)___ .

The group later changed their name to Islamic State of Iraq and Levant for about a year,   before declaring itself to be a worldwide ___E:caliphate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliphate)___ ,   called simply the Islamic State ( الدولة الإسلامية , ad-Dawlah al-Islāmiyya ).
During its rule in Syria and Iraq, the group "became notorious for its brutality".

Under its rule of these regions, IS launched ___E:genocides against Yazidis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazidi_genocide)___ and ___E:Iraqi Turkmen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Turkmen_genocide)___ ; engaged in ___E:persecution of Christians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persecution_of_Christians_by_the_Islamic_State)___ , ___E:Shia Muslims U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persecution_of_Shias_by_the_Islamic_State)___ , and ___E:Mandaeans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandaeans)___ ; publicised ___E:videos of beheadings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_beheadings)___ of soldiers, journalists, and aid workers; and ___E:destroyed several cultural sites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destruction_of_cultural_heritage_by_the_Islamic_State)___ .

The group has perpetrated terrorist massacres in territories outside of its control, such as the ___E:November 2015 Paris attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_2015_Paris_attacks)___ , the ___E:2024 Kerman bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Kerman_bombings)___ in Iran, and the ___E:2024 Crocus City Hall attack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crocus_City_Hall_attack)___ in Russia. ___E:Lone wolf attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lone_wolf_attack)___ inspired by the group have also taken place.

After 2015, the ___E:Iraqi Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Armed_Forces)___ and the ___E:Syrian Democratic Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_Democratic_Forces)___ pushed back IS and degraded its financial and military infrastructure,  assisted by advisors, weapons, training, supplies, and airstrikes by the ___E:American-led coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Inherent_Resolve)___ ,  and later by ___E:Russian airstrikes, bombings, cruise missile attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_intervention_in_the_Syrian_civil_war)___ , and ___E:scorched-earth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorched_earth)___ tactics across Syria, which focused mostly on razing ___E:Syrian opposition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_opposition)___ strongholds rather than IS bases.

By March 2019, IS lost the last of its territories in ___E:West Asia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Asia)___ , although its affiliates maintain a significant territorial presence in Africa as of 2025.

The Islamic State, abbreviated IS,  is ___E:also known as U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Names_of_the_Islamic_State)___ the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL /ˈaɪsɪl/ ___E:EYE-sil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key)___ ), the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS /ˈaɪsɪs/ ___E:EYE-siss U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key)___ ),   and by its ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic)___ acronym Daesh   ( داعش , Dāʿish , .mw-parser-output .IPA-label-small{font-size:85%}.mw-parser-output .references .IPA-label-small,.mw-parser-output .infobox .IPA-label-small,.mw-parser-output .navbox .IPA-label-small{font-size:100%} IPA: [ˈdaːʕɪʃ] ),  and also as Dawlat al-Islām ( دولة الإسلام ).
In April 2013, having expanded into Syria, the group adopted the name ad-Dawla al-Islāmiyya fī l-ʿIrāq wa-sh-Shām ( الدولة الإسلامية في العراق والشام ).

As al-Shām is a region often compared with the ___E:Levant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levant)___ or the ___E:region of Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria_(region))___ , the group's name has been variously translated as "Islamic State of Iraq and ___E:al-Sham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Sham)___ ",  "Islamic State of Iraq and Syria" (both abbreviated as ISIS),  or "Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant" (abbreviated as ISIL).

In 2014, ___E:Dar al-Ifta al-Misriyyah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar_al-Ifta_al-Misriyyah)___ dubbed ISIS as "QSIS" for "al-Qaeda Separatists in Iraq and Syria", arguing that the group does not represent the vast majority of Muslims.

While the use of either one or the other ___E:acronym U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acronym)___ has been the subject of debate,  the distinction between the two and its relevance has been considered less important.
Of greater relevance is the name Daesh, which is an acronym of ISIL's ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language)___ name ad-Dawla al-Islamiyya fī l-ʿIrāq wa-sh-Shām , or Daesh.

This name is widely used among the Muslim world,  as well as ISIL's Arabic-speaking detractors,  for example when referring to the group whilst speaking amongst themselves, although—and to a certain extent because⁠—it is considered derogatory, as it resembles the Arabic words Daes ("one who crushes, or tramples down, something underfoot") and Dāhis (loosely translated as "one who sows discord").
Within areas under its control, ISIL considers use of the name Daesh punishable by ___E:flogging U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellation)___ .
In late June 2014, the group renamed itself ad-Dawla al-Islāmiyya ( lit. ' Islamic State ' or IS), declaring itself a worldwide ___E:caliphate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliphate)___ .

The name "Islamic State" and the group's claim to be a caliphate have been widely rejected, with the UN, various governments, and mainstream Muslim groups refusing to use the new name.  The group's declaration of a new caliphate in June 2014 and its adoption of the name "Islamic State" have been criticised and ridiculed by Muslim scholars and rival Islamists both inside and outside the territory it controls.

In a speech in September 2014, United States president ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ said that ISIL was neither Islamic (on the basis that no religion condones the killing of innocents) nor a state (in that no government ___E:recognises U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_recognition)___ the group as a state),  while many object to using the name Islamic State owing to the far-reaching religious and political claims to authority which that name implies.

The ___E:United Nations Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council)___ ,  the United States,  Canada,  Turkey,  Australia,  the United Kingdom,  and other countries generally call the group ISIL, while much of the Arab world uses the ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic)___ acronym Dāʻish or Daesh.
France's Foreign Minister ___E:Laurent Fabius U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurent_Fabius)___ said: "This is a terrorist group and not a state.
I do not recommend using the term Islamic State because it blurs the lines between Islam, Muslims, and Islamists.

The Arabs call it 'Daesh' and I will be calling them the 'Daesh cutthroats'."  Retired general ___E:John Allen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_R._Allen)___ , the U.S. envoy appointed to co-ordinate the coalition; ___E:U.S. Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)___ Lieutenant General ___E:James Terry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_L._Terry)___ , head of operations against the group; and ___E:Secretary of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State)___ ___E:John Kerry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry)___ had all shifted towards use of the term Daesh by December 2014,  which nonetheless remained a pejorative in 2021.

The ___E:ideology of the Islamic State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ideology_of_the_Islamic_State)___ has been described as being a hybrid of ___E:Salafism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salafism)___ ,   ___E:Salafi jihadism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salafi_jihadism)___ ,     ___E:Islamic fundamentalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_fundamentalism)___ ,  ___E:Wahhabism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wahhabism)___ ,     and ___E:Qutbism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qutbism)___ ,    as well as other doctrines.

According to Robert Manne, there is a "general consensus" that the ideology of the Islamic State is "primarily based upon the writings of the radical Egyptian theoretician ___E:Sayyid Qutb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sayyid_Qutb)___ ".

The Muslim Brotherhood began the trend of political Islamism in the 20th century, seeking gradual establishment of a new ___E:Caliphate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliphate)___ , a comprehensive Islamic society ruled by sharia law. Qutb's doctrines of jahiliyya (pre-Islamic ignorance), hakimiyya (divine sovereignty), and takfir of entire societies formed a radicalized vision of the Muslim Brotherhood's political Islam project. ___E:Qutbism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qutbism)___ became the precursor to all ___E:jihadist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jihadist)___ thought, from ___E:Abdullah Azzam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullah_Yusuf_Azzam)___ to ___E:Zawahiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zawahiri)___ and to Daesh.

Alongside Sayyid Qutb, the most invoked ideological figures of IS include ___E:Ibn Taymiyya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibn_Taymiyyah)___ , Abdullah Azzam, and ___E:Abu Bakr Naji U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_Hasan_Khalil_al-Hakim)___ .

Although IS claims to adhere to the ___E:Salafi theology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athari)___ of ___E:Ibn Taymiyyah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibn_Taymiyyah)___ , it rejects traditional Salafi interpretations as well as the four Sunni schools of law, and anathematizes the majority of Salafis as ___E:heretics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heretics)___ .
IS ideologues rarely uphold adherence to Islamic scholarship and law manuals for reference, mostly preferring to derive rulings based on self-interpretation of the Qur'an and Muslim traditions.

___E:Abu Omar al-Baghdadi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Omar_al-Baghdadi)___ , the first Emir of the ___E:Islamic State of Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq)___ , was radicalised as a Muslim Brotherhood member during his youth.

Motaz Al-Khateeb states that religious texts and Islamic jurisprudence "alone cannot explain the emergence" of Daesh since the Muslim Brotherhood and Daesh "draw on the same Islamic jurisprudence" but "are diametrically opposite" in strategy and behavior.

Through the official statement of beliefs originally released by al-Baghdadi in 2007 and subsequently updated since June 2014, ISIL defined its ___E:creed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aqidah)___ as "a middle way between the extremist ___E:Kharijites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khawarij)___ and the lax ___E:Murji'ites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murji%27ah)___ ".  : 38 ISIL's ideology represents radical Jihadi-Salafi Islam, a strict, ___E:puritanical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_puritanism)___ form of ___E:Sunni Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni_Islam)___ .
Muslim organisations like Islamic Networks Group (ING) in America have argued against this interpretation of ___E:Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam)___ .

ISIL promotes ___E:religious violence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_violence#Islam)___ , and regards Muslims who do not agree with its interpretations as ___E:infidels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kafir)___ or ___E:apostates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostasy_in_Islam)___ .

According to Hayder al Khoei, IS's philosophy is represented by the symbolism in the ___E:Black Standard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Standard)___ variant of the legendary battle flag of ___E:Muhammad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad)___ that it has adopted: the flag shows the ___E:Seal of Muhammad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seal_of_Muhammad)___ within a white circle, with the phrase above it, " ___E:There is no god but Allah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahada)___ ".

This symbolism is said to symbolize IS's belief that it represents the restoration of the ___E:caliphate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliphate)___ of ___E:early Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_history_of_Islam)___ , with all the political, religious and ___E:eschatological U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_eschatology)___ ramifications that this would imply.

Abu Abdullah al-Muhajir, an Egyptian Jihadist theoretician and ideologue is considered as the key inspiration for early figures of IS.    Al-Muhajir's legal manual on violence, Fiqh ad-Dima ( The Jurisprudence of Jihad or The Jurisprudence of Blood ),      was adopted by IS as its standard reference for justifying its extraordinary acts of violence.

The book has been described by counter-terrorism scholar Orwa Ajjoub as rationalising and justifying "suicide operations, the mutilation of corpses, beheading, and the killing of children and non-combatants".
His theological and legal justifications influenced IS,    al-Qaeda,  and ___E:Boko Haram U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boko_Haram)___ ,  as well as several other jihadi terrorist groups.

Numerous media outlets have compared his reference manual to ___E:Abu Bakr Naji U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Bakr_Naji)___ 's Management of Savagery ,     widely read among IS's commanders and fighters.
IS adheres to global jihadist principles and follows the hard-line ideology of ___E:al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda)___ and many other modern-day jihadist groups.
For their guiding principles, the leaders of the Islamic State ... are open and clear about their almost exclusive commitment to the Wahhabi movement of Sunni Islam.
The group circulates images of Wahhabi religious textbooks from Saudi Arabia in the schools it controls.
Videos from the group's territory have shown Wahhabi texts plastered on the sides of an official missionary van.
— David D. Kirkpatrick, The New York Times

According to The Economist , ___E:Saudi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia)___ practices followed by the group include the establishment of ___E:religious police U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_religious_police)___ to root out "vice" and enforce attendance at ___E:Salah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salah)___ prayers, the widespread use of ___E:capital punishment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment_in_Islam)___ , and the destruction or re-purposing of any non- ___E:Sunni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni)___ religious buildings.  ___E:Bernard Haykel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Haykel)___ has described IS leader ___E:Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Bakr_al-Baghdadi)___ creed as "a kind of untamed Wahhabism".
Senior Saudi religious leaders have issued statements condemning IS,  and attempting to distance the group from official Saudi religious beliefs.
What connection, if any, there is between Salafi-Jihadism of IS and Wahhabism and Salafism proper is disputed.
IS borrowed two elements of ___E:Qutbism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qutbism)___ and 20th century Islamism into its version of Wahhabi worldview.
While Wahhabism shuns violent rebellion against earthly rulers, IS embraces political call to revolutions.
While historically Wahhabis were not champion activists of a ___E:Caliphate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliphate)___ , IS borrowed the idea of restoration of a global Caliphate.

Although the religious character of IS is mostly Wahhabi, it departs from the Wahhabi tradition in four critical aspects: dynastic alliance, call to establish a global caliphate, sheer violence, and apocalyptism.

IS did not follow the pattern of the first three Saudi states in allying the religious mission of the Najdi ulema with the ___E:Al Saud family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Saud)___ , rather they consider them apostates.
The call for a global caliphate is another departure from Wahhabism.
The caliphate, understood in Islamic law as the ideal Islamic polity uniting all Muslim territories, does not figure much in traditional Najdi writings.
Ironically, Wahhabism emerged as an anti-caliphate movement.

Although ___E:violence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violence)___ was not absent in the First Saudi State, Islamic State's displays of beheading, immolation, and other forms of violence aimed at inspiring fear are not in imitation of early Saudi practices.
They were introduced by Abu Musab Al-Zarqawi, former leader of Al-Qaeda in Iraq, who took inspiration from the Egyptian Jihadi scholar, Abu Abdallah Al Muhajir.
It is the latter's legal manual on violence, popularly known as Fiqh ad-Dima (The Jurisprudence of Blood), that is the Islamic State's standard reference for justifying its acts of violence.
The Islamic State's apocalyptic dimension also lacks a mainstream Wahhabi precedent.
IS aims to return to the early days of Islam, rejecting all ___E:innovations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bid%27ah)___ in the religion, which it believes corrupts its original spirit.

It condemns later caliphates and the ___E:Ottoman Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire)___ for deviating from what it calls pure Islam and seeks to revive the original Qutbist project of the restoration of a global caliphate that is governed by a strict Salafi-Jihadi doctrine.
Following Salafi-Jihadi doctrines, IS condemns the followers of secular law as disbelievers, putting the current Saudi Arabian government in that category.
